subject: Copywriting
title: Jeff Goodby: Got Milk?
description: A fast breakdown of Jeff Goodby: Got Milk? for builders.

hook.text: Jeff Goodby's 'Got Milk?' campaign turned a declining commodity into a cultural icon. Two words and a milk mustache.

buildup.text: The California Milk Processor Board was desperate. Milk sales had fallen for 20 straight years. Goodby took the brief.

discovery.text: The insight: people only think about milk when they run out. The ads showed moments of deprivation—dry cereal, cookies.

twist.text: Celebrity milk mustache photos became the real campaign. Stars lined up for free. The format became self-sustaining.

climax.text: 'Got Milk?' was licensed, parodied, and became part of the language. It's the most imitated ad format in history.

punchline.text: Two words saved an industry. Got Milk? Got genius.

quiz.question: What insight drove the 'Got Milk?' campaign?
options: People only think of milk when they don't have it

details.summary: Jeff Goodby of Goodby Silverstein & Partners created 'Got Milk?' in 1993, one of the most recognized advertising campaigns in history. The campaign's genius was focusing on the absence of milk rather than its benefits — making people feel the panic of reaching for a glass and finding none.
details.whyItMatters: Got Milk? proved that deprivation-based advertising — making people feel what they'd miss — can be more powerful than benefit-based messaging. It spawned an entire genre of 'Got [X]?' parodies.
takeaways: The campaign focused on the frustration of not having milk
Deprivation framing was more motivating than listing health benefits
'Got Milk?' became one of the most parodied ad phrases in history

faq.question: Why did 'Got Milk?' focus on not having milk?
faq.answer: Previous milk campaigns touted health benefits but failed to increase sales. Goodby's insight was that people don't think about milk until they don't have it — when eating cookies or cereal. The deprivation angle triggered an emotional response that health facts could not.

faq.question: How successful was the 'Got Milk?' campaign?
faq.answer: The campaign reversed a 20-year decline in California milk consumption within its first year. It expanded nationally and became one of the most recognized ad campaigns in history, running for over two decades and spawning countless parodies.
